+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import collections.abc as cabc
+import typing as t
+
+from .core import Command
+from .shell_completion import get_completion_class
+from .utils import echo
+
+
+def strict_completion_status(
+    cli: Command,
+    ctx_args: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any],
+    prog_name: str,
+    complete_var: str,
+    instruction: str,
+) -> int:
+    """Perform shell completion for the given CLI program, like
+    :func:`~click.shell_completion.shell_complete`, but distinguish an
+    unknown shell from an unknown instruction in the status code.
+
+    :param cli: Command being called.
+    :param ctx_args: Extra arguments to pass to
+        ``cli.make_context``.
+    :param prog_name: Name of the executable in the shell.
+    :param complete_var: Name of the environment variable that holds
+        the completion instruction.
+    :param instruction: Value of ``complete_var`` with the completion
+        instruction and shell, in the form ``instruction_shell``.
+    :return: Status code to exit with. ``0`` on success, ``1`` if the
+        shell is not recognized, ``2`` if the shell is recognized but
+        the instruction is not.
+    """
+    shell, _, instruction = instruction.partition("_")
+    comp_cls = get_completion_class(shell)
+
+    if comp_cls is None:
+        return 1
+
+    comp = comp_cls(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var)
+
+    if instruction == "source":
+        echo(comp.source())
+        return 0
+
+    if instruction == "complete":
+        echo(comp.complete())
+        return 0
+
+    return 2
diff --git a/tests/test_strict_completion_status.py b/tests/test_strict_completion_status.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a796371
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_strict_completion_status.py
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+import pytest
+
+from click.core import Command
+from click.core import Option
+from click.shell_completion import shell_complete
+from click.strict_completion_status import strict_completion_status
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def cli():
+    return Command("cli", params=[Option(["--name"])])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("instruction", "expect"),
+    [
+        ("bash_source", 0),
+        ("zsh_source", 0),
+        ("fish_source", 0),
+        ("bash_unknown", 2),
+        ("bash", 2),
+        ("bash_", 2),
+        ("unknown_source", 1),
+        ("", 1),
+        ("_source", 1),
+    ],
+)
+def test_status(cli, capsys, instruction, expect):
+    assert strict_completion_status(cli, {}, "cli", "_CLI_COMPLETE", instruction) == (
+        expect
+    )
+    strict_out = capsys.readouterr().out
+    shell_complete(cli, {}, "cli", "_CLI_COMPLETE", instruction)
+    assert strict_out == capsys.readouterr().out
+
+
+def test_complete_matches_shell_complete(cli, capsys, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("COMP_WORDS", "cli --")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("COMP_CWORD", "1")
+    assert (
+        strict_completion_status(cli, {}, "cli", "_CLI_COMPLETE", "bash_complete") == 0
+    )
+    strict_out = capsys.readouterr().out
+    assert shell_complete(cli, {}, "cli", "_CLI_COMPLETE", "bash_complete") == 0
+    assert strict_out == capsys.readouterr().out
+    assert "--name" in strict_out
notes:
Added strict_completion_status mirroring shell_complete via get_completion_class, returning 2 only for an unrecognized instruction on a recognized shell; tests compare status and output against shell_complete.
